crops.name: Miscanthus (elephant grass)
crops.ireland: Suits the south and east; check DAFM bioenergy supports.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.5–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Low needs after establishment; slurry or sewage-sludge use is not permitted under organic rules (sludge) — use FYM/compost.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.5–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Rain-fed; willow tolerates wet ground well.

harvest.storage: Chip and air-dry; store under cover.

conventional.pests: Weeds in year 1 are the main risk; willow rust and leaf beetle.

organic.pests: Thorough pre-planting weed control (cultivation), mixed clones for willow, mulch.
organic.weeds: Repeated cultivation before planting, mechanical weeding in year 1.

crops.rotation: Perennial (willow harvested every 3 years for ~20 years; miscanthus 15–20 years).

crops.name: Flax (fibre)
crops.overview: Historic Irish linen crop, now niche.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: High N demand is hard to meet organically: grow after clover-rich ley or legumes and apply slurry/FYM in spring. Sulphur from permitted elemental S or gypsum.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.critical: Flowering and pod fill (Apr–June for winter OSR).

conventional.pests: Cabbage stem flea beetle, pollen beetle, slugs, light leaf spot, phoma, sclerotinia. Spray only above thresholds.

organic.pests: Sow early into good seedbeds for vigour, companion crops (e.g. buckwheat/berseem) to confuse flea beetle, wide rotation (1 in 5) against clubroot and sclerotinia.
organic.weeds: Wide rows with inter-row hoeing; competitive early canopy.

crops.rotation: 1 year in 4–5 (clubroot). Excellent break crop before wheat.

crops.name: Reed canary grass

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Clover provides ~100–150 kg N/ha/yr in a good sward. Spread slurry/FYM in spring; lime to pH 6.3+. Permitted rock phosphate where P index 1–2.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 5.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Grass growth in Ireland is usually limited by temperature, not water, except on light soils in dry summers.
water.critical: May–August soil moisture deficits slow growth, especially in the south-east.

harvest.storage: Silage: wilt to 25–30% DM, roll and seal well; bales wrapped 6 layers.

conventional.pests: Leatherjackets and frit fly after reseeding; rust in autumn. Herbicide for docks/thistles/chickweed at reseeding.
conventional.weeds: Post-emergence herbicide 4–6 weeks after reseeding (clover-safe products if clover sown).

organic.pests: Multispecies and clover swards, good grazing management, topping and hand-pulling docks, avoid poaching.
organic.weeds: Mowing/topping before weeds seed, dock digging, competitive sward.

crops.rotation: Leys of 3–7+ years; reseed after tillage or when sward is poor.
